customer-jon: Hey team, hitting a reproducible issue with the Python SDK streaming API — the generator yields a partial token (starts with 'Th') and then stalls indefinitely. Happens ~20s into the stream every time. Using SSE mode.
sarah-support: Sorry you're seeing this, can you paste the minimal repro and SDK + python versions? Also any small logs around the hang would help. :pray:
customer-jon: Repro below. Python 3.10.12, redwood-sdk==0.13.0. Code:```py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=...)
for chunk in client.chat.stream(model="gpt-open-unrolled", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"write a short story"}]):
    print(chunk)
```
Logs when it stalls:```
SSE recv: b'data: {"id":"evt_1","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Th' }
SSE recv: b'\n'
# generator yields 'Th' and then nothing else, connection stays open.```
sarah-support: Thanks. Can you also share whether you see periodic keepalive heartbeats (empty `data: \n` events) from the server?
customer-jon: Yes, we see keepalives about every 10s. The hang coincides with a keepalive arriving right after a fragmented `data:` chunk.
devon-eng: @customer-jon this points to a boundary-handling bug in the SSE parser — when a `data:` line is split across two TCP chunks and a heartbeat (`data:\n`) interleaves, the parser can treat the partial `data:` as complete and return an incomplete delta. Can you run a quick `pip freeze`?
customer-jon: pip freeze:```
redwood-sdk==0.13.0
httpx==0.24.0
anyio==3.8.0
```
sarah-support: Filing an internal ticket. @devon-eng can you triage? ci-bot: Ticket created: SUP-4821 — "Python stream stalls on keepalive boundary (partial data chunk)" (link: https://internal.redwood.ai/t/SUP-4821)
devon-eng: Thanks. Quick workaround: set `client.stream_heartbeat_timeout=5` (reduces interval the client uses to coalesce chunks) or disable keepalives on the server side if possible. We'll ship a parser patch.
customer-jon: Workaround helped, stream resumed but still occasionally yields 1-2 char prefixes before finishing.
alex-ml: Can you paste a raw hex of the chunk sequence when it stalls? That will confirm the interleaving. Example we want to see `b'data: {\"delta\": {\"content\": \"Th'` followed immediately by `b'\ndata: \n'` etc.
customer-jon: Here's a pasted sequence (sanitized):```
0000: 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 64 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 20 7b  "data: {\\"delta\\": {"
0010: 22 63 6f 6e 74 65 6e 74 22 3a 20 22 54 68        "content": "Th"
001d: 0a 64 61 74 61 3a 20 0a                             .data: .
```
devon-eng: Perfect — that matches. Root cause: the SSE handler treated the `\n` as event delimiter and emitted the event early even though `data:` content was not complete. We'll update the parser to buffer across heartbeat events when an open `data:` line is not terminated by a full JSON object.
ops-luis: For mitigation on customers using older SDKs: we recommend pinning redwood-sdk>=0.14.2 once released, or using the HTTP streaming fallback (non-SSE) by setting `stream_mode='raw'` in the client constructor.
sarah-support: ETA for fix? @devon-eng
devon-eng: I'll push a fix to master today and target a 0.14.2 patch release by EOD tomorrow. Patch summary: robust SSE boundary scanning, stricter UTF-8 chunk reassembly, and tests that simulate keepalive interleaving.
customer-jon: Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround. Any temporary debug setting we can enable to auto-retry on generator stalls?
devon-eng: Add a small wrapper:```py
def stream_with_retry(gen, timeout=30):
    last = time.time()
    for item in gen:
        last = time.time()
        yield item
        if time.time() - last > timeout:
            raise RuntimeError('stream timeout')
# then recreate client.stream() if exception
```
This is crude but works as a short-term client-side recovery.
sarah-support: Marking this thread as escalated. We'll message you when 0.14.2 is published. :thumbsup:
customer-jon: Great, I'll test the patch when available and report back.
